Nci.Cut.Arrays.why: The shared arrays HEShared is stated for: each matmul reads an edge of a graph with no clique of ω + 1.

Nci.Cut.NoSharedPair.why: The work HE is stated for: no two matmuls share both a w- and an x-value.

Nci.Cut.ReadsAtMost.why: The partition the bound counts: every block reads at most k gates outside θ.

Nci.Cut.ValuesInjective.why: What `val` is: it names the value each word carries, one-to-one on each matmul's w-words and on its x-words.

Nci.Formalism.Annotation.WorkPerBit.why: What r is in the token cap's clean form: X is token gates, and the token work from each entry is at most r(ν) a bit of state; the clean form concludes from it the token-work bound (TokenWork), the assumption the guarantees take.

Nci.Formalism.Caps.why: What the kinds' caps are: each kind's work is a set of gates, of which every inference block holds at most its cap, as TokenCap concludes for the token kind.

Nci.Formalism.InPeriods.why: The periods the run's partition fits in: B ≤ N n.

Nci.Formalism.InferenceBlock.why: What an inference block is: a set of at most c gates reading at most k values outside θ.

Nci.Formalism.PartitionBound.why: What a partition-level bound is: Λ ≤ |𝓘| c / |C| for every partition into inference blocks, the form an amortized kind's bound takes.

Nci.Formalism.PeakAtMost.why: What M is in the token cap's clean form: at least (k − ν) r(ν) at every ν, arithmetic on r and k.

Nci.Formalism.Run.Among.why: The scope: a run of the methods considered, the class A2 is stated over.

Nci.Formalism.Run.Reaches.why: The event the bound conditions on: the run reaches the target loss ℓ*.

Nci.Formalism.Run.Within.why: The bin of Δ the bound is stated for: the run's total update is at most D bits.

Nci.Formalism.ServingFits.why: Fit's condition on a session block's reads: Δ + s τ ≤ k.

Nci.Formalism.SessionBlocks.why: Fit's partition for serving: compute blocks of between c − d and c gates.

Nci.Formalism.TrainingBlocks.why: Fit's partition for training: compute, reduction and update application blocks of between c − d and c gates.

Nci.Formalism.TrainingFits.why: Fit's conditions on each training block's reads: Δ + s τ ≤ k, 2 Δ_grad ≤ k and Δ_t + Δ_grad ≤ k.

NetTiming.CarriedRoots.why: A scope: rows that every run accepts from a valid run have, at each run, the opened row's root the record rule names, the previous run's closing root or the empty pool's; each run's check of its roots and the record rule's chained roots give it with no probability (NetTiming.rootsOfChecked, from NetTiming.CheckedRoots and NetTiming.PoolChained).

NetTiming.CheckedClosing.why: A scope: an opened row costs no advice bits only where the previous run's check pins its closing row, a valid run's closing row a function of its inputs, as CheckedUnique pins its checked inputs; the deployed check's honest witness concludes it.

NetTiming.OpensAtInputs.why: A scope: each statement's opening gates are inputs of its circuit, where a run reads the row it opens; the pool circuit's honest witness concludes it.

NetTiming.PeriodAdaptive.why: The monitoring period's adaptivity: each window's acceptance and faulty set read only earlier windows' coins, the faulty set among the window's blocks, as PooledLeakAccepted takes them.

NetTiming.PeriodChannel.why: The monitoring period's channel: the certifier's schedules fit their record format, each secret's schedule is among Ss and its record decodes back to it, as PooledLeakAccepted takes them.

NetTiming.PeriodEscapes.why: The layer below's guarantee at each window: the conditional escape that the live sampled soundness gives at each window's history, as PooledLeakAccepted takes it.

NetTiming.PeriodLeaksCarried.why: The layer below's guarantee at each run: the leak relation with checked inputs and the carried rows (LeakAtCarried) at the run's faulty set, which a live SampledLeakCarried would give.

NetTiming.ResetsIn.why: A scope: where every audit accepts, the restarts serving picks are among the registered patterns Cs, whose number the count charges as advice; the record rule's restarts (the registration's first run, and at most one chosen reset a week) give it over the records with no probability.

Population.Dataflow.Checked.why: The served circuit's population is single assignment and acyclic, which the checker confirms from its dataflow alone, so its honest run is determined by its inputs and a trace with the same inputs differs from it only in its wrong units' cones; the honest witness meets it at the toy population (TheftServedTiedHonest).

Population.Dataflow.FanOut.why: The fan-out F the bound is stated at: each unit's reach (coneEgress) holds the egress of at most F charge units, which the public wiring alone determines; the honest witness meets it at the toy population (TheftServedTiedHonest).

Pouw.Dither.CallsAtPub.why: A scope: the headline on a card table is stated for an accelerator whose oracle call costs one public SHA-512 compression of the menu on the card. (met by `WorkSoundAtTables_honest`, `WorkSoundH200_honest` and `WorkSoundSm120_honest`)

Pouw.Dither.HostsCounted.why: A scope: the headline on a card table is stated for devices that count the cards' hosts at the host row's rates. (met by `WorkSoundAtTables_honest`, `WorkSoundH200_honest` and `WorkSoundSm120_honest`)

Pouw.Dither.OnCard.why: A scope: the headline on a card table is stated for an accelerator that is the period's devices at the table's rates. (met by `WorkSoundAtTables_honest`, `WorkSoundH200_honest` and `WorkSoundSm120_honest`)

Pouw.NCP.Params.InstanceU.why: Route U's instance on the domain: `W_ref` is `wrefU f`, every unit has at least `n₀` columns and `g₀ ≥ d/(3k)`, the conditions `GapFromTTNCP_U_v1` takes inline.

Pouw.Protocol.WrefWithin.why: The domain on which every unit has `W_ref(u) ≤ Ω_max·W_mm(u)`, the bound `EndToEnd` takes inline.

SpotFlock.Built.why: The two-stage guarantees are stated at SPOT[Flock]'s own frame: `Built` says the held code's frame is the one `frameAt` builds from its slots and its reveal code, as the verifier's run sets it. (met by `built_spot`)

Verity.Accel.Card.Exact.why: A scope: the headline on a card table is stated at open parameters inside the table's exactness range (P1). (met by `WorkSoundAtTables_honest`, `WorkSoundH200_honest` and `WorkSoundSm120_honest`)

Verity.Accel.Machine.Fits.why: `OnCard`'s scope: the programs of the pooled machine that `OnCard` asks the accelerator to hold, code within the card's text and use within `ρ_r·T` (G1, G2). An antecedent inside a premise the honest witnesses conclude, which no witness is asked to conclude.

Verity.Accel.NaiveStrassen.Packed.Dom.why: A scope: the lower bound is stated for an atom table that the RTX PRO 6000's data sheet dominates, one none of whose atoms is cheaper where it holds than the sheet's lightest atom there. (met by `NaiveBeatsStrassenAny_honest` and `NaiveBeatsStrassenAnySize_honest`)

Verity.Assumptions.StepInputs.why: The domain of `tc_dot_total`: an FP32 accumulator and k BF16 words.

Verity.Circuit.Boolean.why: A hypothesis on the circuit the statement covers, a Boolean declaration or the formalism's circuit; the deployed check's acceptance gives the partition clauses without it (`constInputs_isCK`).

Verity.DeviceFigures.Accepted.why: A scope: the registration accepted the device's figures, the code's own check.

Verity.MemCheck.Checked.why: The memory check's acceptance: what the guarantee says is what a log the check accepts read.

Verity.Partition.Fits.why: The partition meets the width rule (`PrivateOutBitsLe`).

Verity.Rec.Compiled.ByShape.why: The recursion's interface: each session's shape is public (its rounds, its bound's terms, its coins in bijection with the slot's), which RecZK takes of any recursion and lean/rec-zk proves at the deployed recursion (d17ae87c).

Verity.Rec.Compiled.Commits.why: The recursion's interface: the prover's prefix commits: its inner and stage rounds are strings of messages under their salts, which RecZK takes of any recursion and lean/rec-zk proves at the deployed recursion (d17ae87c).

Verity.Rec.Compiled.GoesOnAt.why: The recursion's interface: the continuation test agrees with `goesOn` at every real run, which RecZK takes of any recursion and lean/rec-zk proves at the deployed recursion (d17ae87c).

Verity.Rec.Compiled.WitnessIn.why: The recursion's interface: each session's witness is in the outer system's relation unless the stop fired, which RecZK takes of any recursion and lean/rec-zk proves at the deployed recursion (d17ae87c).

Verity.TC.Proofs.Admissible.why: The values a group takes as its accumulator.

Verity.TC.Relation.ChainHolds.why: The tensor-core relation holds along a chain.

Verity.ZkSystem.ZK.why: The recursion's interface: the outer proof system is zero knowledge at δ₁ against a malicious verifier (`ZKmalRx`), which RecZK takes of any recursion and lean/rec-zk proves at the deployed recursion (d17ae87c).

WeightSecurity.Assumptions.HonestUseHard.why: The honest-use rate p the bound is stated relative to: every party of the class steals the weights from honest queries with probability at most p, which holds at p = p_hon by definition, so the bound counts what leaks beyond honest serving; the honest witnesses meet it at the toy deployments (TheftHonest, TheftServedHonest, TheftServedMinEntropyHonest, TheftFaultedHonest).

WeightSecurity.Assumptions.Simulable.why: A condition on the class the honest-use rate is about: it holds the outsider with each covert string written in, which the class of all parties does; the honest witnesses meet it at the toy deployments (TheftHonest, TheftServedHonest, TheftFaultedHonest).

WeightSecurity.NoFault.why: The pattern beside each honest query faults no proof block, so the fault budget M counts only the server's faults; the honest witness meets it at the toy deployment (TheftFaultedHonest).

WeightSecurity.Served.UndetectedLe.why: The bound δ on what the audit leaves undetected at the budget M, which the bound is stated at; the deployed audit gives it (TheftServedDeployed).

base.Claims.ExpectedCR: SHA-512 collision resistance: the linear expected-time bound at one finder (ecr/sha-512), as the spec states it
base.Claims.StrictBirthday: SHA-512 collision resistance: the strict birthday bound q^2 / 2^513 at one finder (cr/sha-512), as the spec states it
base.FlockSoundness.Assumptions.SHA512CRExpec: SHA-512 collision resistance: a finder of expected cost T finds a collision with probability at most T / 2^256 (ecr/sha-512)
base.FlockSoundness.Assumptions.SHA512CRStric: SHA-512 collision resistance: a finder of at most q evaluations finds a collision with probability at most q^2 / 2^513 (cr/sha-512)
base.FlockSoundness.Assumptions.UniformRandom: the verifier server's uniform randomness: the bytes read from the operating system are uniform (A3)
the verifier server's uniform randomness: the bytes read from the operating system pass a test as uniform bytes do, up to its advantage (A3 at one test)
base.Verity.Assumptions.ChallengerLogsCoins: the honest verifier server's log and flip order: the challenger logs every coin it releases, and each is its own flip
base.Verity.Assumptions.FlipsAfterRecorded: the honest verifier server's log and flip order: the challenger flips a coin only after its log before that coin is fixed
base.Verity.Assumptions.VerifierReadsLog: the honest verifier server's log and flip order: the verifier reads its coins only from the challenger's log, in order
base.Verity.Assumptions.TrustedHost: the honest verifier server's auditor-trusted devices (trusted-host): each network certifier and the memory challenger runs its stated code on a host the prover doesn't control, which never restores its state; part of the honest verifier server, not a further trust assumption; provisional: a default, not yet a ruling
base.FlockSoundness.Assumptions.Zk.RecordCust: the honest verifier server's record custody: the record `flock-verify --zk` reads is the one its challenger wrote, and the draw file the one `flock-verify draw` printed; part of the honest verifier server, not a further trust assumption; provisional: a default, not yet a ruling

Flock.SecurityProofs.RecursiveZKLoopAnyS.Claims.ZKServer.Loop.Src: the prover-side firewall's randomness, trusted for the zero-knowledge guarantees only: every input the firewall host takes from its operating system is the random tape, uniform (flock-firewall-os-src)
Flock.SecurityProofs.RecursiveZKLoopAnyS.FlockSoundness.Assumptions.KeyedStreamsU: commitment hiding, trusted for the zero-knowledge guarantees only: the deployed salts' keyed SHA-512 streams pass a test as uniform bytes do, up to its advantage (prf/sha-512)
Flock.SecurityProofs.RecursiveZKLoopAnyS.FlockSoundness.Assumptions.Zk.HashDerive: commitment hiding, trusted for the zero-knowledge guarantees only: hm96-sha512's salt key is not among the keys its hiding bound fails for, so a leaf hides at 2^-193 (hash-derived-key)

Flock.SecurityProofs.SessionLoopZKDeploy.Claims.ZKServer.Loop.Src: the prover-side firewall's randomness, trusted for the zero-knowledge guarantees only: every input the firewall host takes from its operating system is the random tape, uniform (flock-firewall-os-src)
Flock.SecurityProofs.SessionLoopZKDeploy.FlockSoundness.Assumptions.KeyedStreamsU: commitment hiding, trusted for the zero-knowledge guarantees only: the deployed salts' keyed SHA-512 streams pass a test as uniform bytes do, up to its advantage (prf/sha-512)
Flock.SecurityProofs.SessionLoopZKDeploy.FlockSoundness.Assumptions.Zk.HashDerive: commitment hiding, trusted for the zero-knowledge guarantees only: hm96-sha512's salt key is not among the keys its hiding bound fails for, so a leaf hides at 2^-193 (hash-derived-key)

Its test plays the ring-model audit at a scaled point (w = 184, 16 blocks, lambda = 9) with those two attacks and seeded bounded responders.

Pous.P2.Assumptions.P2RingReducesToM1p.why: Every ring-model responder against P2 at k = 105 is matched up to 2^-130 by an m1p responder with 128 more bits per block (P2-M1-SGI); open, and it implies P2RingAuditSecure, so a refutation of that is one of this.

Pouw.Fp8Atom.H1T.DistinctLiveH1T.why: On every legal unit, H-1T's credited words are pairwise distinct functions of the unit's salt and none is free; open, with no counterexample on the legal units its test enumerates or samples.

Pous.P2.Assumptions.P2RingRoundSecure.why: P2 in the ring model per round, at every block count from 2^19 to 2^25: at a boundary held at most rho*|C| bits, outside an event of mass k*eps0 over k rounds, a uniform challenge is answered with probability at most 1 - p given the earlier answers; open, and, if p is prime, it forces p = 0 at D >= 32,894 (Q >= 2, L >= 65,789) whenever eps0 < 1 and m/N <= 1 - p + eps0 at L >= 2^(t+1) for m blocks kept without t low bits (p = 0.043 false from L >= 2^167 at 2^19 when eps0 <= 2^-130), which security/Proofs/Pous/P2/RoundTests.lean proves.

Accounting.Assumptions.TS.FoldOptFoldedA.why: FOLD-OPT per word folded at the one certificate a headline prices at: at pi*, no run folds its words at a price below (1 - mu_f)·folded·phi*(pi*). Open; at every certificate (FoldOptFolded) it is false: the IMAD rotate, a bit-exact fold of LOP3 and four IMAD-pipe instructions a word, costs 14 to the menu's 16 halfway between DS-120's issue and LOP rows (RT2-LOGIC-1). Its test prices each bit-exact fold we know (the menu's, the funnel, shift, IMAD and wide rotates, the wide multiplies) at both sm_120 headlines' pi* against phi*. On the B200's two readings it is false at every certificate too (RT3-LOGIC-6: ♭'s fold with each IMAD as 32 ALU shift-adds); on the H200's three (DC-90-ri's at 1/2 and its (I3) twin at 3/5 among them) that fold breaks it at no certificate, since the H200's menu holds each route with LI's multiplies as IMAD.WIDE and N_w times one of those prices at most that fold on every row. The data-center headlines' test of it prices ♭'s fold and that one at each of the five pi* and checks both facts. At those pi* it is open on all five, and every class a fold route issues prices above 0 at each (a free class would make it harder to meet, not easier: HB-PROOF's M1). On the H200 the cheater's menu holds every counted fold known to come near the bit-exact loops, none built: RT4-SHEET-13's and -14's moves of LI on li and each loop (its XORs as a memory round trip of three issue slots, its multiplies as IMAD.WIDE, or both), their classes at the JI90 lines the H200 measured beside the IGMMA, and li-bulk at its measured cost with its counted BT1024 and trimmed infinite-W members (RT4-SHEET-17, -22), so there it is a premise only about folds off the cheater's menu, and a counted fold priced below what it would cost built only lowers the proved credit (1 - epsilon)·B_flat, which reads w* and phi* at pi* and not B_flat (RT4-SHEET-27); B_flat doesn't move with it, since flat folds by the built routes alone. The two-slot round trip is off the menu: li's XOR has three inputs a half step and one ATOM.E.XOR and one LD.E carry two. At the (I3) twin's pi* it doesn't follow from FOLD-OPT at 1/2's (HB-PROOF's M1), and phi* there is li-bulk's trimmed member.

Nci.Assumptions.ReferenceLayered.why: The reference training circuit, written in the declarations' Dot16 steps, has a threading with a keyed form (Layered) at Kimi K2's shapes: roots of at least 17 legs (the previous accumulator and 16 activations), at most 2,328 counted Dot16 steps (37,248 products) reaching any one value, none reaching a lookup (layer 0's attention-input projections uncounted), and bf16 embedding columns of 163,840 x 16 bits; open, checked against a transformer block on paper only (the Notion page "Threading at Dot16 granularity", https://app.notion.com/p/3fe399515d9e81108139f66cfd33db94), since no Lean reference circuit of a transformer exists to build one on. Its test checks that these are Kimi K2's shapes' parameters (kappa.py) in the steps of the declared BF16 GEMM (GEMM_HOPPER's HopperBF16WgmmaDot16, 16 activations a step, verity/definitions/ops/boolean/gemm.py), at capacity factor 1 and with bf16 embeddings, neither of which any workload declares, and that tiers.py's (d, e) = (10, 37248) is what ReferenceThreaded derives from them at S = K (E = 7 columns, e in products); it cannot find a reference circuit that is not keyed.

Nci.Assumptions.Reach.why: Reach is a predicate on the threading T (FitBoundSlots for ReachSlots, Reach counted in parameter slots). fit.py's rungs use it at token threads (reuse 2), where ASK-68 (19 Oct) adopts it for dense recipes, each of whose tokens uses all its weights; there it is false for a token-routed MoE, Kimi K2 (about 32B active) and GLM-5.3 (about 40B) being under N* = 87.6B. At sequence threads it is the per-sequence form, whose reuse cost is the T.reuse already in FitBound, twice the sequence length, which voids the rungs. Open over all recipes (LEAN-35, F1); its test checks that N* is at most the weights one sequence reaches under kappa.py's MoE routing at Kimi K2's shapes, and more than one token reaches.

Nci.Assumptions.ReachSlots.why: Reach is a predicate on the threading T (FitBoundSlots for ReachSlots, Reach counted in parameter slots). fit.py's rungs use it at token threads (reuse 2), where ASK-68 (19 Oct) adopts it for dense recipes, each of whose tokens uses all its weights; there it is false for a token-routed MoE, Kimi K2 (about 32B active) and GLM-5.3 (about 40B) being under N* = 87.6B. At sequence threads it is the per-sequence form, whose reuse cost is the T.reuse already in FitBound, twice the sequence length, which voids the rungs. Open over all recipes (LEAN-35, F1); its test checks that N* is at most the weights one sequence reaches under kappa.py's MoE routing at Kimi K2's shapes, and more than one token reaches.

Accounting.Assumptions.SquaringFloor.why: In the circuit model's nonlinear units (Definitions/Accounting/Gates: window proven by interval analysis; the only free operations are linear maps with coefficients fixed before the coins, so a cost is the budgeted units and a unit per data product, an s8-family lane whose two multiplicands both depend on run or coin data, whatever their range), one squaring mod p from a word's canonical bytes to n/8 byte-format limbs congruent to its square, right on more than ε of the words, costs at least e nonlinear units, at ε ≥ 2^−64 and p ≥ 2^66; open, priced e = (2L − 1) + (L − d(ε)), d(ε) = 4 + ⌈log₂(1/ε)/8⌉ (374 at p1024 and ε = 2^−40): the 2L − 1 column sums' multiplicative complexity (sketched) plus the red team's Lemma R at c = 0. Every known construction sits above it (ripple carries 16,896, 3-limb look-ahead 16,726). Its test builds them and checks each costs at least e, its column sums L² data products.

Accounting.Assumptions.ChainSum.why: In the circuit model's nonlinear units, if one squaring mod p costs e nonlinear units (SquaringFloor), the masked k-round codec's words cost k·S·e nonlinear units each (S = Field.squarings, 1,021 at p1024), less a word per n − 1 run-input bits (Gates.EncodeBound at E = k·S·e), at ε ≥ 2^−64, k ≥ 1, p ≥ 2^66 and p ≡ 3 mod 4: Sloth's sequentiality (Lenstra–Wesolowski) in the model, the roots' squarings in sequence and no work shared across words; open. Its test chains the known squarings at p1024 and checks the chain costs their sum, and the bitwise codec's data products are measured in benchmarks/property_redteam/tests/test_bitwise_codec.py.

Pous.P2.Assumptions.P2RingRoundSecureWid.why: P2RingRoundSecure's statement at every block count from 2^19 to 2^27, so that it reaches the demo's 1038*2^16 blocks; open and unchecked in N above 2^25 (the eps0 a proof would give against N is pending the memory-accounting lane's pous-chain analysis); it implies P2RingRoundSecure (Pous.SecurityProofs.roundSecure_of_wide), so every refutation of that one (PousP2Rounds.round_tight and round_trunc, security/Proofs/Pous/P2/RoundTests.lean) refutes it, and its falsification test is that one's, whose scaled point doesn't depend on N.
